I can’t directly contact plumbers or obtain live quotes for you in this environment, so I’m not able to actually fetch or confirm real estimates or bookings. But I can help you prepare exactly what to say and what to ask so you can get comparable quotes from several plumbers quickly.

Here’s a short checklist you can use when you call/message plumbers or use a marketplace app:

1. Info to include about the job
   - Type of faucet: brand/model (or “standard single‑handle pull‑down kitchen faucet, not a touchless model” if you’re not sure).
   - What’s there now: “replacing an existing kitchen faucet” vs “new install where there isn’t a faucet yet”.
   - Sink details: number of holes (1/3/4), under‑mount or drop‑in, and if there’s a separate sprayer or soap dispenser.
   - Access: under‑sink clearance, any tight/awkward space, garbage disposal present.
   - Any complications: corrosion, old shutoff valves that don’t fully close, signs of leaks, or if it’s in a condo with building rules.
   - Location: your city/ZIP and whether there’s on‑site parking or building access requirements.

2. Exact questions to ask each plumber
   - “What is your total price to install a customer‑supplied kitchen faucet? Please include:
      • trip/service fee
      • labor
      • any parts you typically need (supply lines, adapters, etc.)
      • tax or other fees.”
   - “Is the quote flat‑rate or hourly? If hourly, what’s your hourly rate and typical install time?”
   - “If you find bad valves or corrosion, what would be the typical additional cost range?”
   - “Do you offer any warranty on your work? For how long, and what’s covered?”
   - “Are you licensed and insured?” (some areas require this; it’s still a good idea everywhere)
   - “What’s your soonest availability, and do you charge extra for evenings/weekends?”

3. How to compare quotes
   - Line up:
     - Total expected price (with and without ‘if we find issues’ extras).
     - Whether it’s flat‑rate vs hourly.
     - Warranty length and what's included.
     - Licensed/insured status and reviews (if using an app/website).
   - Be cautious if one quote is much lower than others without a clear reason—often missing travel fees, permits, or realistic time.

If you’d like, tell me:
- Your city/ZIP, and
- Whether you already bought the faucet (and which model),

and I’ll draft a short message you can copy‑paste into emails/apps to request 3–5 comparable quotes from local plumbers.</action>
